chapter: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
title: Bands using Fletcher's name: Rainbow Orchestra, Andrade, and the Stompers
summary: Horace doubts anyone used Fletcher's name regularly, says Vernon Andrade's Renaissance band was separate, and that the Stompers name merged his and Fletcher's men for records.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Okay. "To summarize"-- I'm quoting here --"there were five essentially different groups which accepted engagements either using Fletcher Henderson's name or implying his sponsorship." Here's one, "Fletcher Henderson and his Rainbow Orchestra, led by violinist Ellsworth Reynolds, spring 1925 into 1926." Does this mean anything to you? I couldn't quite understand it.
It doesn't ring a bell with me. Where did they play?

The only time that I know something like this transpired, and I think I'm pretty well correct in it. Fletcher wouldn't give anybody permission to use his name for a long period of time. I know some things that have happened like this. Fletcher has had two jobs in one night, casuals, when he has designated some guy to front the band until he could get there, but this was an agreement made between the promoters and Fletcher. But for a guy to play a regular job stating -- no way. No. Because I've done the same thing, I've had two jobs, in one night, too, and you've done it, too.
I remember New Year's Eve, man, in Fort Collins.
Vernon Andrade's Andratti's orchestra possibly working under the name Dixie Stompers.

No, that's incorrect, 1000 percent incorrect. Vernon Andrade's Andratti's was the house band always at the Renaissance Ballroom at 138th and 7th Avenue in New York City, and he played for different club dates. This was all he did, and he was the banjo player in the band. And the leader -- and he had a regular group there that played all these things, all these jobs with him, and his band didn't record, and they went under the same name of -- as Vernon Andrade Andratti's and his Renaissance Ballroom Band.

Uh-huh. I see. Okay. Here we have Horace Henderson's Wilberforce Collegians, which we've talked about, sometimes billed as Fletcher Henderson's Stompers. Now it says here, "Basically, Horace's college band with Rex Stewart, Benny Carter, Freddy Jenkins, et cetera, about 1925 to spring, 1928." I remember asking you about this before, and you said that the Stompers was a name that was used for recording purposes.
And that it did sometimes involve a combination of your personnel and some of Fletcher's.
But we never went by that name steady. We didn't drop the agents Collegians (unintelligible), but the Stompers, the reason we arrived at that name is because it constituted the members of both bands.
